summary: Raghunath Damodar Karmarkar (1893–1964) worked in Indology and philosophy. He was former principal of Sir Parashurambhau College and served as Director of the Post-Graduate and Research Department (attested 1953) and professor (attested 1966) at Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.
Raghunath Giri was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Vamacharana Bhattacharya. He held a position as section head at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.
Raghunath Purushottam Paranjpye (1876–1966) studied under Vaman Shivram Apte. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1959).

Rahul Peter Das (born 1954), an Indologist and linguist, studied at Cologne and Hamburg under Klaus Ludwig Janert and Albrecht Wezler. He taught and researched at Hamburg, Bonn, Groningen, and Marburg, and was Professor der Südasienkunde at Halle-Wittenberg (1994–2020).

Rahul Sankrityayan (1893–1963) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He held a Sanskrit teaching position at Vidyalankara Pirivena (1927) and taught Sanskrit at Saint Petersburg State University (1937), where he later held a professorship (1945–1947).

Raimo Anttila (1935–2023) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Yale University under Warren Crawford Cowgill (~1962–1966) and held posts at the University of California, Los Angeles (1965) and the University of Helsinki (1971–1976).

Raimon Panikkar (1918–2010), a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology, earned doctorates from Madrid under Juan Zaragüeta and Lateran University. He taught at Complutense University of Madrid, Harvard University, and the University of California, Santa Barbara (1971–1978; emeritus ~1987–2010).

Raimond Gaita (born 1946) is a philosopher who studied at the University of Melbourne and the University of Leeds. He served as Professor of Moral Philosophy at King's College London (1977–2011) and Foundation Professor of Philosophy at Australian Catholic University (1993–2011).

Rajan Gurukkal (born 1948) works in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at the University of Calicut and Jawaharlal Nehru University, he served as Director of the School of Social Sciences at Mahatma Gandhi University (1988) and taught at JNU.

Rajeev Sangal works in computational linguistics and Indology. Educated at IIT Kanpur and the University of Pennsylvania, he held posts at IIT Kanpur (1982–1998), IIIT Hyderabad (2002–2013, 2018–2022), and IIT (BHU) Varanasi (2013–2018).

Rajendra Chandra Hazra (1904–1982) was an Indologist who completed his doctoral studies under Sushil Kumar De. He held lecturing posts at Jagannath University (1931) and the University of Dhaka (1939–1951), and was Associate Professor at Sanskrit College (1951–1972).

Rajendra Mishra (born 1943) is an Indologist who studied under Rambhadracharya. He has served as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, head of the Sanskrit department at Himachal Pradesh University, and visiting professor at the University of Indonesia.

Rajendralal Mitra (1824–1891) was an Indologist and historian. He served as director of Wards' Institution (1856–1881) and held posts at The Asiatic Society as librarian-cum-assistant-secretary (1846–1856) and president (1885).

Rajesh P. N. Rao (born 1970) works in computational fields and Indology. He studied under Dana H. Ballard at the University of Rochester and joined the faculty at the University of Washington, serving as Professor of Computer Science from 2000.

Rajkrishna Mukhopadhyay (1845–1886) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Krishnagar Government College and Presidency University (~1864–1868). He held academic posts at Scottish Church College and Presidency University (~1878–1880).

Rakhal Das Banerji (1885–1930), a historian and Indologist, studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta. He was an officer at the Archaeological Survey of India (1911–1926) and held the Manindra Chandra Nandy professorship at Banaras Hindu University (1928–1930).
Rakra Tethong Rinpoche studied under Gendün Chöphel (~1946–1951) and Trijang Rinpoche.

Ralf Kramer (born 1971) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and at the University of London, later serving as Aris Librarian for Tibetan & Himalayan Studies at the Bodleian Library (~2003–2008).

Ralph Abraham (1936–2024), a philosopher and mathematician, studied at the University of Michigan and under Debabrata SenSharma. He held posts at Berkeley, Columbia, and Princeton, and served as Associate Professor (1968) and Professor (1980) at UC Santa Cruz.
Ralph Lerner (born 1928) is a philosopher who studied at the University of Chicago (~1947–1953) under Leo Strauss. He subsequently held a post at the University of Chicago from ~1953 to 2003.
